controlled_change: Proposed isolated two-to-four-row gate/up kernel with one output channel per SIMD group. No precision, router, single-row, down-projection, reduction, cache, or scheduling changes.
correctness: The new candidate is unimplemented. The selecting command and counter captures independently match all 128 outputs, full logits, proposal/recovery decisions and persistent target/draft state. Both cover the same routes, geometry, and 23087 dispatches.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: The clean current counter window ranks 2124 multi-row gate/up calls at 27.476ms per committed output. This is an instrumented inclusive ranking, not a projected or attainable request saving.
hypothesis: Sharing gathered input loads and BF16-rounded affine bias sums between gate and up can reduce multi-row routed-expert GPU work while retaining separate exact accumulators.
limitations: No kernel candidate or speed improvement is implemented by this evidence stage.
2606 adjacent counter intervals overlap; sums are not exclusive request latency.
Only 16 committed outputs of one 128-token coding workload are profiled.
The memory-disturbed LRU capture and earlier rejected single-row packed-Q4 experiment contribute no timings.
outcome: Two clean interval-merging captures peak below 9.747GiB. Generic Q8 hyper projections rank at 14.503ms and GDN scan at 2.121ms. The next protocol selects the larger multi-row gate/up scope for a cheap operator screen.
smallest_experiment: Independent real-weight exactness for 2/3/4 rows and gathered orders, then five fresh alternating operator pairs within 256MiB. Advance only at >=10ms median frequency-weighted GPU saving and an upper paired ratio below one; a survivor still needs fresh normal-request timing.
